decision_scope: current approved access, venue, cohort and scientific contract

facts: The provider documents hourly files, history beginning 2025-06-28, and approximate availability fifteen minutes after each hour.
Liquidation files are sparse by design and exist only when the venue published at least one liquidation event for the symbol and hour.
Public liquidation broadcasts may be throttled or sampled, so their totals are lower bounds.
Complete prefix listing requires short-lived S3 credentials generated after dashboard login.
The fixed nine-object sample verified row structure and immutable hashes but did not prove complete historical coverage or historical archive availability.
blockers: No anonymous complete prefix inventory or immutable full-period manifest is available.
Guessing every REST path would be a rate-limited brute-force substitute for a complete listing and cannot distinguish an unavailable object from a collection outage.
Approximate hour-plus-fifteen-minute availability is not per-object historical publication proof.
The verified sample contained open-interest snapshots received up to about 41.7 hours after their exchange timestamps, so event time cannot be backdated into decision time.

facts: The official open-interest statistics endpoint documents only the latest one month of data.
The official market-data catalogue does not provide a public historical forced-liquidation endpoint equivalent to the required cohort.
blockers: One month of open-interest history cannot cover the frozen interval.
The required historical forced-flow family cannot be reconstructed from current or user force-order endpoints.

facts: The official public archive exposes USDⓈ-M mark-price klines and metrics/open-interest style files with dated objects.
The reviewed public daily and monthly USDⓈ-M catalogues do not expose an equivalent historical liquidation-event family.
blockers: Price and open-interest archives cannot replace the predeclared forced-flow input without changing the economic hypothesis after selection.

reopen_conditions: A complete CryptoHFTData prefix inventory plus immutable SHA-256 hashes and historical receipt semantics is supplied under already-authorized access.
A zero-cost source is found that preserves the same Binance USDⓈ-M instruments, frozen interval, received-time chronology and lower-bound forced-flow semantics.
The Lead selects a materially distinct available-data hypothesis under a new frozen fingerprint.
